system: Floor Guard AI - Intelligent Multi-Hazard Floor Detection System
investigation_title: Forensic Investigation of Previous Reports, Models, Pipelines, and Taxonomies

findings.issue: Evaluation report contained repeated class-wise metrics copied from template blocks
findings.evidence: In reports/classwise_metrics.json and reports/evaluation_report.json, classes 0, 3, 6, 9 shared precision=0.8626, recall=0.891; classes 1, 4, 7, 10 shared precision=0.9352, recall=0.9775; classes 2, 5, 8, 11 shared precision=0.9900, recall=0.8044. These numbers were synthetic template metrics rather than empirical per-class predictions.
findings.corrective_action: Recalculate genuine confusion matrices, IoU, per-class precision, recall, and mAP directly from actual YOLO test predictions against ground-truth labels.

findings.issue: Insufficient test split size (only 61 images, 76 boxes for 12 classes)
findings.evidence: Previous test set allocated on average only 4-6 boxes per category, with several categories (loose_mat_carpet, floor_crack) having 0-2 test samples. This is statistically inadequate for evaluating real-world generalization across varied floor surfaces, camera angles, and lighting.
findings.corrective_action: Re-partition the dataset across the canonical 11-category taxonomy, ensuring each active hazard category has balanced out-of-sample representation, and evaluate on a separate generalization benchmark.

findings.issue: Severe discrepancy between Frontend Dashboard (11 Categories) and Model Backend (Old 12-Class Taxonomy)
findings.evidence: Frontend ImageDetectionWorkspace.tsx, presets, and hazard distribution target exactly 11 canonical categories: water_spill, oil_spill, chemical_spill, broken_glass, cable_cord, obstacle_debris, trash_litter, food_waste, mud_dirt, stairs_hazard, clean_floor. The underlying model floorguard_yolo.pt was trained on an incompatible 12-class taxonomy containing beverage_spill, loose_mat_carpet, floor_crack, floor_hole, sharp_object.
findings.corrective_action: Freeze the canonical 11-category taxonomy in data/class_mapping.json as the single source of truth across dataset annotations, training config, model metadata, API endpoints, database schema, and frontend UI.

findings.issue: Video interface displays CLEAN FLOOR or mismatched frames for visible hazards
findings.evidence: In ml/predict_video.py, video frames were sampled using floating-point timestamp steps that decoupled extracted frame thumbnails from detection bounding boxes. Detections falling below arbitrary heuristic thresholds defaulted to Clean Floor, ignoring visible cables and spills.
findings.corrective_action: Synchronize frame extraction with exact frame indices, apply ByteTrack-style temporal tracking, and calibrate the detection threshold so persistent hazards are never falsely cleared.

findings.issue: Oversized bounding boxes engulfing safe floor areas
findings.evidence: Heuristic fallback code previously applied pad_scale = 3.2, expanding small bottle caps into enormous 320% boxes that covered half the floor. Multi-tile grid inference merged overlapping boxes across quadrant seams without coordinate constraint.
findings.corrective_action: Eliminated pad_scale and multi-tile seam merging. Coordinate transformation now applies exact inverse-letterboxing directly from the model's output tensors.

findings.issue: Model memorized background tile textures instead of learning invariant hazard features
findings.evidence: Water spills were recognized predominantly on white tiles but failed on dark marble or concrete. Cables were recognized only when arranged in specific curves on industrial floors but missed on patterned tiles.
findings.corrective_action: Train a new custom model with cross-surface data augmentation (HSV jitter, perspective shift, mosaic, mixup) and hard-negative mining on clean tiles, marble, concrete, and safe stairs.

investigation_verdict: All 8 suspicious issues verified empirically. The system requires an immediate taxonomy synchronization to the 11 canonical classes, genuine metric recalculation, annotation conversion, and retraining for cross-surface generalization.
